$$\int 3 \cdot \operatorname{atan}(2x) \, dx$$

Here, $\operatorname{atan}(u)$ denotes the **inverse tangent function**, i.e., $\arctan(u) = \operatorname{atan}(u)$. So we are integrating $3 \arctan(2x)$.

---

### Step 1: Recognize the integrand
We want to compute:
$$
\int 3 \arctan(2x) \, dx
$$

This is a standard integral of the form $\int \arctan(kx) \, dx$, but with a constant factor. We can use integration by parts or known antiderivatives.

---

$$
\int \arctan(2x) \, dx = x \arctan(2x) - \frac{1}{2} \ln(x^2 + (1/2)^2) \quad \text{(if scaled appropriately)}
$$
